renderer.name: LibreOffice
renderer.stabilization: Exact-hash source copy and LibreOffice profile were placed under a short no-space temporary path; SAL_DISABLESKIA=1 was set for this conversion.

findings: All 58 pages were inspected at original raster detail.
No unreadable clipping, overlapping text, missing content, missing glyphs, or broken table borders were found.
Emoji and checkbox glyphs render visibly in the applicable chapters.
LibreOffice page 14 shows one continued bullet line with atypical indentation; the text remains present and readable.
LibreOffice page 49 contains one further-reading bullet on an otherwise mostly blank page; the link text remains present and readable.

attempt_history.renderer: direct LibreOffice conversion using the stabilized no-space profile/source-copy path
attempt_history.reason: The exact-hash copy converted successfully in 22.4 seconds and produced the recorded 58-page PDF.

comparison.method: Full source-render inspection plus representative source-to-web semantic, structural, and responsive visual comparison.

cases.observations: Vocabulary row order, meanings, examples, and the contiguous a-MEN-i-tees pronunciation are preserved. Desktop shows the full table; mobile keeps the page at viewport width and contains the wide table in its own horizontal scroll region.
Subject, greeting, paragraphs, three-item detail list, next step, sign-off, author line, and explanatory note preserve the source order and wording without clipping or artificial run breaks.

Receptionist/guest labels remain attached to their dialogue, and the explanatory paragraph plus apology-letter heading, salutation, body paragraphs, sign-off, and author line preserve source wording and sequence.

intentional_adaptations: The browser experience uses responsive cards, section navigation, and application typography rather than reproducing Word pagination.
Wide source tables use a keyboard-focusable horizontal scroll region on narrow screens instead of shrinking text or overflowing the page.
Interactive exercise controls and answer-reveal behavior are application experiences; the comparison does not require them to resemble Word's static print layout pixel-for-pixel.
comparison.conclusion: The representative web sections are faithful semantic and structural projections of the exact-hash source. No material omission or source-order inconsistency was found in the compared content.

limitations: LibreOffice is not Microsoft Word; pagination, font metrics, and list indentation can differ slightly between rendering engines.
All 58 source pages were inspected, but browser screenshot comparison is representative rather than a screenshot pair for every one of the 85 web sections.
This technical visual review does not replace the open qualified accessibility, ESP/CEFR, hospitality-practitioner, link, retention, and content-owner release gates.
